claim.pdf_says: Index entries printed one per line with sub-entries indented beneath their main entry, e.g. 'CHARACTERS' followed by the indented sub-entry 'BLOCK CONTAINS clause, VII-23'
claim.markdown_says: Every entry is a bare line with no list marker, sub-entries only space-indented: 'CHARACTERS' then '  BLOCK CONTAINS clause, VII-23'
claim.why_it_matters: Markdown renders consecutive bare lines as one paragraph, so the whole index page collapses into one run-on line and the entry boundaries and main-entry/sub-entry hierarchy are lost in the rendered document (pages 961-962 use '- ' list items and keep them). The entries and page references themselves match the PDF; the index is informative, not normative.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered PDF page 963 (index page B-51) and page-963.md checked: every entry and page reference read matches (e.g. Character set, IV-4 / Restriction, VI-1; CHARACTERS with BLOCK CONTAINS clause VII-23, INSPECT statement VI-94, MEMORY SIZE clause VI-11, RECORD clause VII-30; CLOSE statement sub-entries; Comma sub-entries). The markdown keeps one entry per line and two-space indentation for sub-entries, so the text and hierarchy are present in the source. The claim concedes the content matches; its only point is that Markdown renderers merge bare lines into a paragraph and that pages 961-962 use '- ' list markers. That is a formatting and consistency difference in the transcription's presentation, not a content discrepancy against the PDF, and it does not change the meaning of any entry. Under the verification rules (reject formatting-only differences), not real.
